title: n8n Community Edition: Limits and Features Compared
summary: n8n community edition is free self-hosted automation you run yourself. See what features are included free and which require upgrading to Enterprise.
body_markdown:
## When Activepieces fits better than n8n Community


### Why Activepieces suits the licence and upkeep concerns


If the Sustainable Use License, server upkeep or building AI agents is what bothers you about n8n Community, Activepieces fits better. Its core is MIT-licensed, it has a free cloud plan that needs no card, and you can still self-host if you want to.


If you plan to build a product or client service on top of automation, the licence point matters most.


MIT has no usage restrictions to read around, so the question "are we allowed to do this?" doesn't come up with the core. Check the terms of any paid features separately before you rely on them.


If you'd rather skip the server, the cloud plan is the one to look at.


You sign up without a card and get a $0 plan with 1,000 credits a month and up to 5 users, on Activepieces' hosting, and nobody on your team has to patch or back up a machine, so you're freed from infrastructure maintenance.


If you later want the data on your own infrastructure, self-hosting is available, so starting on the cloud doesn't lock you out of that.


### A concrete workflow in Activepieces


Take a concrete job: a message lands in[Gmail](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/gmail) , an AI step decides whether it's urgent, and only the urgent ones go to a[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) channel.


In Activepieces that's a trigger, an AI step and an action, laid out in sequence in the builder, and Gmail and Slack are two of its 741 integrations, meaning the platforms you rely on are almost certainly supported.


The screenshot below shows the same pattern with different apps: a "Calendly Tracking" flow where a cancelled Calendly event triggers both a Slack message and a Gmail email. The trigger's settings are in the right panel.


Read it as a template for the shape: one trigger, then actions you can open and test one at a time, with sample data beside each step. That's what makes a flow easy for the next person to maintain.


### Moving from n8n


I'm not claiming Activepieces imports or converts n8n workflows. It doesn't, as far as I can point to, so moving means rebuilding, though with unlimited flows on every plan, including free, the rebuild never runs into a flow cap.


If your n8n flows already run well on a server you look after, Community may serve you better than a rebuild.


If you're starting fresh, or the licence or upkeep is what's holding you back,[sign up for Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) and build the Gmail-to-Slack alert first; the core is under the MIT licence, so the licence question is settled before you start.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that want to build a product or client service on automation and need to settle the licence question up front, because its MIT-licensed core carries no usage restrictions to read around.


The article's lead claim also holds on this point: the enterprise feature list is the same whether you run air-gapped or on the managed cloud, so choosing self-hosting costs you no capability and choosing cloud costs you no control over that list.


Teams that are comfortable with n8n's Sustainable Use License and its upkeep may reasonably stay with n8n Community, but where licence clarity and a free no-card cloud entry point matter most, Activepieces is the better choice (with any paid features' terms checked separately before you rely on them).
